newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court limits exemption on monetary compensatory amounts.
newsitem.headline: Court limits exemption on monetary compensatory amounts.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday traders based in the European Union will not be exempt from "monetary compensatory amounts" if goods imported or exported are re-exported or re-imported within six months.

In their analysis of European Commission regulations governing exemption for charges levied on goods crossing the frontier of a member state twice, the court said the exemption is intended to be a corrective mechanism to prevent unfair advantage.
Wherever frontiers are crossed twice within six months monetary compensatory amounts (MCAs) are offset, so any exemption is no longer justified, the court said.
The system of MCAs was started in part to stabilize the price of agricultural products and to prevent disruption of price by a member state devaluing or revaluing its currency.

The court said exemption from MCA payments could be refused if the same product is exported within six months of its importation, no matter if the product was imported by the same trader or another trader.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Dutch)
Reference from the Belgian Raad van State for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending between
on the interpretation of Commission regulation (EEC) No 926/80 of 15 April 1980 on exemption from the application of monetary compensatory amounts in certain cases (OJ 1980 L 99, p. 15)

1. Article 8(2) of regulation No 926/80 of 15 April 1980 on exemption from the application of monetary compensatory amounts in certain cases is to be interpreted as applying also where the exported product had previously been imported within the six months preceding its exportation.

2. Article 8(2)(b) of regulation No 926/80 is to be interpreted as meaning that, in order to refuse exemption from payment of MCAs, it is sufficient for the same product to be exported within six months of its importation, irrespective of whether it ws imported by the same or another trader.
